content.title: We Were Once Their Whole World
content.subtitle: How Much of Their World Are We Today?
content.body:
When we were children, our world was small, and our parents filled almost all of it. They knew when we were hungry, stayed awake when we were sick, and held us when we were afraid. They understood our needs before we could express them.

Then we grew up. Education, jobs, marriage, family, children, life created a world of our own. Our responsibilities grew, our lives became busier, and somehow, the time we had for our parents began to shrink.

Once, We Wanted Their Time

Remember? When Dad was late from work, we would wait by the door. When Mom was busy in the kitchen, we would ask, “Mom, how much longer?” Back then, their time and attention meant everything to us.

Today, we need no excuse to call Dad or sit beside Mom. Yet strangely, the people we once longed to be near now have to wait for us to find the time.

We Are Growing Up, They Are Growing Old

As our parents grow older, their world becomes smaller. Their bodies weaken, familiar faces become fewer, and they go out less. Meanwhile, their wait for their children seems to grow longer.

We think, “I’ll visit when I have time.” But their age does not wait for our time. One day, perhaps we really will have time. No office, no busyness, no excuses.

Only the person we wanted to give that time to may no longer be there. Mom’s number may still be in our phone, but her “Hello, Baba” may not be. Dad’s old chair may still be there, but Dad may not.

Parents Are More Than Our Responsibility

Parents are a blessing whose value we often understand only when we fear losing them.

So today, let us put aside our busyness and call our parents. If possible, let us sit beside them. Let us listen patiently, even when they repeat the same things. When we were little, they listened to us countless times and forgot their own needs for us.

So, let us make a little space in the world of those who once filled our entire world.
